summary: Backend iteration 2 testing: discount logic, full invoicing module, lifetime pro. 19/19 new tests pass after fixing one critical bug. Found and fixed MongoDB ObjectId serialization issue in /api/quotes/{id}/convert-to-invoice.

critical.issue: Returned 500 on first call: ValueError [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable"), TypeError('vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute')]. After motor's insert_one(inv), pymongo mutates dict to include _id, then FastAPI failed to serialize ObjectId. Fixed by inv.pop('_id', None) before return. Subsequent (idempotent) calls returned 200 because they short-circuited via existing-invoice lookup with {_id:0} projection.

minor.issue: sent_at update_one runs unconditionally even when Resend send fails (sent_ok=False, error present). Consider only setting sent_at when sent_ok is True for accurate audit.
Endpoint converts ANY quote regardless of status. Spec implies UI shows convert button only when status='accepted'; backend has no guard. Could be intentional but should be documented.
Lifetime is gated by hardcoded set LIFETIME_PRO_EMAILS rather than configurable env / DB-managed list. Hard to extend.

action_items: Bug fix already applied: pop _id from inv dict in convert-to-invoice endpoint (server.py line ~751). Main agent should review and keep this fix.
Optional: gate convert-to-invoice on status='accepted' if business logic requires it (currently any status allowed).
Optional: only set sent_at when Resend send succeeds (avoid recording sent_at on failures).
Optional: make LIFETIME_PRO_EMAILS configurable via env or DB.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:751 BUG (FIXED): motor's insert_one mutates the inserted dict to attach ObjectId _id; the original code returned that dict, causing JSON serialization 500. Pattern to follow throughout: always pop('_id', None) after insert_one before returning, OR build a clean response dict.
server.py:766-770 update_invoice does not guard against changing status->'unpaid' wiping out previous paid_at; idempotency around state transitions could improve.
server.py:914 CORS allow_origins falls back to '*' with allow_credentials=True which browsers reject. Ensure CORS_ORIGINS env is set in production to explicit origins.
server.py file is 937 lines - approaching the 700-line guideline; consider splitting into modules: auth.py, quotes.py, invoices.py, billing.py, pdf.py.
build_pdf does not handle missing client_name/email gracefully (would KeyError). Inputs are required by Pydantic so OK for now but defensive .get() would be safer.

_mark_overdue mutates the doc in-memory only — actual DB document never gets persisted as 'overdue'. This is fine for read paths but stats and listings recompute every call (small perf concern at scale).

Invoice number format INV-YYYY-NNN confirmed. Convert-to-invoice is idempotent and carries over discount fields. Past-due auto-flips status on GET (DB doc unchanged). Free plan limit (3 quotes) does NOT count invoices. Auth isolation works (404 across users). Send invoice succeeded with real RESEND_API_KEY for the test domain used. Bug fix applied: convert-to-invoice now pops _id before returning - confirm this remains.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: motor (async pymongo) insert_one() mutates the input dict in-place to add the generated _id field (an ObjectId). The convert_quote_to_invoice handler returned the same dict directly, so FastAPI's response serialization received an ObjectId which is not JSON-serializable. Reproduction: POST /api/quotes/{any-quote-id}/convert-to-invoice -> first call 500 (insert path returns mutated dict), second call 200 (idempotent path re-fetches from DB with {_id:0} projection). Mitigation: `inv.pop('_id', None)` before `return inv`. Same pattern should be audited everywhere insert_one's input is returned; existing code already does this correctly for /api/clients (line 318) and /api/quotes (line 390).
